chunks: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babuwayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated to us. He said: Bakr ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan ibn Ziyad al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Hakam narrated to us. He said: Mansur ibn Abi al-Aswad narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said:

When the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) became ill with the illness in which Allah took his soul, his Ahl al-Bayt and his companions gathered to him and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, if something were to happen to you, who will be for us after you? Who will take charge of your authority over us?' But he did not give them any answer, and remained silent regarding them.

On the second day, they repeated the question to him, but he did not respond to them about anything they had asked. On the third day, they said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, if something were to happen to you, who will be for us after you? Who will take charge of your authority over us?' He said to them: 'Tomorrow, a star will descend from the sky into the house of a man from my companions. Look for who he is, for he is my vicegerent over you after me, and the one who will take charge of my authority over you.' And there was not one among them except that he desired that the Prophet would say to him: 'You are the one who will take charge after me.'

On the fourth day, each man among them sat in his room, looking for the descent of the star, when suddenly a star fell from the sky, its light overpowering the light of the world, until it landed in the room of Ali (peace be upon him). The people became agitated and said: 'By Allah! This man has gone astray and is misguided, and he does not speak regarding his cousin except by desire.' So Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed regarding that:
'By the star when it descends! Your companion is neither misguided nor astray, nor does he speak from desire. It is but an inspired revelation.' (53:1-4) to the end of the surah.

key_terms.أهل بيته: the People of the House, referring to the Prophet's household
key_terms.القائم: the one who takes charge, the person entrusted with authority
key_terms.الهوى: personal desire or whim, what the Prophet was falsely accused of following
key_terms.خليفة: vicegerent, successor appointed to carry out authority
key_terms.نجم: star, the celestial sign that indicated divine designation

ai.seo_question: What is the occasion of revelation (shan al-nuzul) of Surah al-Najm according to Shia hadith about the star falling on Ali's house?
ai.summary: This narrative recounts events during the Prophet Muhammad's final illness. Over three days, his household and companions asked who would succeed him. On the third day, the Prophet said a star would fall from the sky into the house of his successor. On the fourth day, a brilliant star descended into the room of Ali ibn Abi Talib, provoking the people to accuse the Prophet of speaking from personal desire about his cousin. In response, Allah revealed the opening verses of Surah al-Najm (53:1-4), affirming that the Prophet was neither misguided nor speaking from desire, but conveying divine revelation.
